quality.title: Data quality
quality.intro: This page is a feature, not an apology: it lists openly what the archive knows, what it is unsure of and what it does not know at all.
quality.tierConfirmedDesc: The archive gives a position and the Wikipedia record does not contradict it.
quality.tierDisputedDesc: The Wikipedia infobox record disagrees with the archive’s position; in most cases Wikipedia lists several positions.
quality.tierUnverifiedDesc: The archive itself has no position. Guessing one would fabricate a third of the dataset; the gap is shown as “unknown”.
quality.disputesIntro: Each row shows the archive’s reading, the Wikipedia field that caused the disagreement, and the verification script’s suggestion.
quality.birthIntro: Players whose birth year is “-” in the source pages; none of them was given an estimated year.
quality.collisionsIntro: When two different Wikipedia titles reduce to the same slug, the second record takes a “-2” suffix; both stay on record.
quality.alsoSearchLinks: {count} rows carry a Wikipedia search link instead of an article; the search query is preserved as part of the identity.
quality.alsoStandBy: {count} rows are the unnamed “stand-by” blocks of the source pages, disambiguated with country and sequence suffixes.
quality.alsoShared: {count} players appear in the squads of two countries.
quality.alsoConflicts: {count} players have conflicting metadata between their country records; the record with a known position and birth year was preferred.
quality.alsoEditions: The 1959 Copa América was played twice in one year; the two tournaments carry “-1” and “-2” suffixed ids while the year stays 1959.

about.title: About
about.scope: Football Matrix gathers the World Cup, continental championship and Olympic men’s football squads of {countries} national teams into a single matrix: players down the rows, tournaments across the columns, shirt numbers in the cells. The archive spans {span}.
about.method: The site reads the canonical dataset produced by a one-time extraction from a hand-built archive of 20 HTML pages; it does not regenerate, modify or re-derive the data. The extraction is verified lossless by automated checks; corrections are made on the dataset with a cited Wikipedia source.
about.sources: Squad records are taken from the English Wikipedia tournament squad pages; retrieved {date}. Olympic note: since 1992 the men’s football tournament is a U-23 competition apart from a limited number of permitted over-age players; earlier eras played under different eligibility rules.
about.positions: Positions are presented in three confidence tiers: confirmed, disputed, unverified. No unknown field is ever guessed; gaps are written out as “unknown” and listed one by one on the data quality page.
about.site: A static site: no analytics, no telemetry, no cookies, no third-party requests. The typefaces — Newsreader, IBM Plex Sans, JetBrains Mono — are licensed under the SIL Open Font License and served from this site. English is the default language, Turkish the second.
